findings.title: The background refresh single-flight drops a reindex that lands mid-refresh
The semantic lane coverage gate opens the read-write database handle from the recommend path
The Ollama-unavailable early return reports zero failures
The coverage check re-reads every SKILL.md on each scored prompt

traceabilityChecks.summary: The feature-catalog page describes the background refresh; the single-flight drop and the read-write handle are not described there.
The review target is a file list, not a spec folder, so there is no checklist.md to check evidence against.

noveltyJustification: All four findings are new: no prior iteration exists in this lineage, and each cites a line the reviewed commits introduced or changed.
classifications: correctness: 2 P1 (lost update in the refresh scheduler, read-write handle from the recommend path) and 2 P2 (outage failure count, per-prompt corpus read)

ruledOut.direction: The refresh can overlap a watcher reindex's database writes
ruledOut.reason: indexSkillMetadata is synchronous and runs before the refresh is fired; better-sqlite3 serializes writes in-process

ruledOut.direction: The refresh can leak the single-flight slot
ruledOut.reason: the finally block clears the slot only when it still holds this refresh

ruledOut.direction: The coverage gate scores a stale vector
ruledOut.reason: embeddingCoverage().complete is false whenever any row is stale or missing and the lane returns []

frontierProposals.question: Does the skillDir filter in refreshSkillEmbeddingsViaAdapter leave rows that embeddingCoverage counts as incomplete forever, so coverageComplete can never become true?
Can refreshCommandEmbeddings prune a live command vector when the bridge projection is momentarily partial, and does the prune run before the outage check?
Does the daemon startup refresh run before the first skill index completes, so it sees zero skill_nodes and never retries after the index lands?
